s07.client_chat.cc_001: My name is Aoife Conneely. My mother is Máire Conneely and in 2017 she pleaded guilty to stealing forty-one thousand three hundred euro from the post office she ran for twenty-one years.
s07.client_chat.cc_002: I was nineteen. I sat in the second row of that courtroom and I believed every word of it, and I have believed it for nine years.
s07.client_chat.cc_003: Last month I read about a woman in Wexford whose conviction was overturned. Same system. Same wording in the charge sheet. Same everything.
s07.client_chat.cc_004: So I asked my mother. She said, and I am quoting her exactly: do what you like, Aoife, I am too old to be told again that I am a liar.
s07.client_chat.cc_005: She still has the same phone. She never got a new one and she has never deleted anything on it, and she has said I can give you access to it. It is live — it is sitting on the table between us and things still arrive on it.
s07.client_chat.cc_006: I want you to find the money. That is the actual job. Forty-one thousand three hundred euro went somewhere and if she took it, I will know, and I will stop.
s07.client_chat.cc_007: I need to be honest that I am not sure which answer I am hoping for, because one of them means I owe her nine years. Will you look?
s07.client_chat.cc_008: Thank you. Start with the photographs. There are hundreds of them and they all look like the same picture and I never once asked her what they were.
s07.client_chat.cc_009: One thing. If it turns out she did take it, you tell me, not her. She has had enough people tell her things.
s07.interstitial.is1_001: Nowhere. You are telling me it went nowhere.
s07.interstitial.is1_002: I have her bank, the credit union, the shop float, my uncle's account and the house. Eleven weeks and the largest thing that moves is a hundred and forty euro for an oil delivery.
s07.interstitial.is1_003: So where does forty-one thousand three hundred euro go, if it does not go anywhere? Keep going. I want the actual answer, not the comforting one.
s07.interstitial.is2_002: She wrote the word down after every call because she thought she was going mad and wanted a record of what she had been told. Sixty-one calls. Isolated, isolated, isolated.
s07.interstitial.is2_003: And Bríd Sheridan was fourteen miles up the road with the same hole in her accounts two years earlier, paying it out of her own savings so that nobody would ever have to use that word about her.
s07.interstitial.is2_004: I have known Bríd since I was five. I do not know what to do with that yet. Keep going.
s07.interstitial.is3_002: Eleven fault reports, one engineer, and a defect with a name, sitting in a document eight months before my mother stood up in a courtroom and said the word guilty.
s07.interstitial.is3_003: I rang her an hour ago. I did not tell her what I had. I asked her why she stopped taking the photographs and she said, because there was no point in counting a thing nobody was going to read.
s07.interstitial.is3_004: One more. I want the name of somebody who had that document and told her to pay anyway.
s07.closing_chat.cl_001: Declan Moran. Area manager, western region. The fault list went to every area manager in the country on the eighth of September 2016 and he opened it, because the read receipt is in her own mailbox on a thread he copied her into by accident.
s07.closing_chat.cl_002: Eight months later he told her to make it good by the Friday.
s07.closing_chat.cl_003: I have not slept properly since Tuesday and I want to say something before we do the practical part.
s07.closing_chat.cl_004: She photographed that safe four hundred and sixteen times. Every night for over a year. She was building this and nobody ever asked her what she was doing, including me, and I lived in the house.
s07.closing_chat.cl_005: Right. My solicitor says there are three things I can do with what you have found and I have to pick one, because they do not go together.
s07.closing_chat.cl_006: One. File it with the Court of Appeal. It is the only thing that removes the conviction. It takes two to four years and she is sixty-three and she says she will not sit in another courtroom.
s07.closing_chat.cl_007: Two. Give the lot to Eibhlín Ní Chonaill, who has been on this four years and will publish inside a fortnight. Fast, loud, and it clears my mother's name in the only place my mother actually lives, which is a village of nine hundred and forty people.
s07.closing_chat.cl_008: But it names Bríd. It has to. Bríd's silence is half the proof that the company knew, and Bríd is sixty-eight thousand euro out of her own pocket and still behind that counter and has done nothing wrong except be as frightened as my mother was.
s07.closing_chat.cl_009: Three, and this is the one my solicitor thinks is soft.
s07.closing_chat.cl_010: I take it to my mother first. All of it, the photographs, the fault list, Moran's read receipt, and I do whatever she says. Including nothing. She might say nothing. She is entirely capable of saying nothing.
s07.closing_chat.cl_011: I have to decide tonight because Eibhlín's editor wants an answer. What do I do?
s07.closing_chat.cl_011.opt1: File the appeal. Get the conviction off her.
s07.closing_chat.cl_011.opt2: Give it to the reporter. Clear her in the village.
s07.closing_chat.cl_011.opt3: Take it to your mother and abide by what she says.
s07.closing_chat.cl_013: The court, then. The slow one.
s07.closing_chat.cl_014: She will hate it and she will do it, because she is the woman who counted a safe four hundred and sixteen times for nobody.
s07.closing_chat.cl_015: Eibhlín, then. I will ring her tonight and I will ring Bríd first, which is going to be the worst phone call of my life and I am not going to make somebody else make it.
s07.closing_chat.cl_016: My mother can walk into that shop again. That is the thing I am buying and I know exactly what I am paying for it.
s07.closing_chat.cl_017: Her, then. I will drive down in the morning and put the whole lot on the kitchen table.
s07.closing_chat.cl_018: Nine years ago a room full of people decided what happened to her without asking her a single question. I am not going to be the last one to do that, even if I am right.
s07.closing_chat.cl_019: Thank you. I came here to find out whether my mother was a thief and instead I found out what she was doing every night at twenty to twelve, and I am going to be a long time getting over that.
s07.ending.court:
The application went to the Court of Appeal in the October. It took three years and one month.

The conviction of Máire Conneely was quashed in November 2029 on the grounds that the prosecution had failed to disclose material bearing directly on the reliability of the evidence — specifically fault report MER-2016-0114, defect OVERNIGHT, and the eleven duplicate reports filed against it before her trial. The judgment names Declan Moran twice. The court's language about the company's disclosure is the coldest in the judgment and is quoted in every article written since.

She did not attend. She had said she would not sit in another courtroom and she did not, and Aoife sat in the second row on her own, in the same seat.

Seventy-four other convictions have since been referred on the strength of the same document. Bríd Sheridan, who was never prosecuted and therefore has no conviction to quash, has recovered none of her sixty-eight thousand euro and is not eligible for the compensation scheme, because the scheme is for people who were charged.

Máire is sixty-six. She has been back to Cloghmore twice, both times to the graveyard, both times on a weekday morning when the shop is shut.
s07.ending.press:
The piece ran across four pages on a Saturday and led the radio news for two days. It carried the photograph of the safe from 14 March 2016 alongside the terminal reading from the same night, and after that nobody in Ireland needed the rest of the article explained to them.

Cloghmore took eleven days. On the twelfth, the shutter of the shop went up for the first time in nine years, because the man who bought the building put a table outside it and about two hundred people came, and Máire Conneely stood at the door of her own post office and shook hands until her arm hurt. Aoife's note that evening was one line: she is not a woman who cries, and she did not, but she could not let go of Peadar's hand.

The conviction still stands. Nothing published in a newspaper removes a conviction, and the appeal has not been filed, and at sixty-three she says she does not care what a file in Dublin says about her.

Bríd Sheridan is named in paragraph nine. She left the counter at Letterfrack in the February and moved to her sister's in Roscommon. She has not answered Aoife's calls. Aoife has kept ringing, once a week, and says she intends to keep ringing.

Declan Moran took early retirement four days after publication.
s07.ending.mother:
Aoife drove down on the Saturday morning and put four hundred and sixteen photographs, one fault list and one read receipt on her mother's kitchen table, and then sat there for two hours while Máire went through them in order without saying anything.

What Máire said at the end of it is recorded, because Aoife had left a voice memo running on the table and has never been able to bring herself to delete it. She said: I knew. I want you to understand that I always knew. What I did not know was whether anybody was ever going to.

She took a fortnight. Then she said yes to the newspaper, no to the court, and one condition on both, which was that Bríd Sheridan was to be telephoned by Máire herself before a word was printed. That call lasted fifty minutes. Neither woman has said what was in it. They are back to speaking every Tuesday.

The piece ran in the spring. The village turned out. The conviction still stands and Máire has said she will consider the appeal when she is ready and not before, which Aoife has stopped pushing.

What changed most is not on any record. Máire started photographing the safe again — the new one, in the shop at Letterfrack, where she does two mornings a week behind Bríd's counter. She says it is a habit and there is no harm in it. Aoife thinks it is something else and has not asked.

s07.mail.gm_001.subject: Branch 4471 Cloghmore — outstanding position
s07.mail.gm_001.body:
Máire,

As discussed on the phone. The position as at close of business Friday is a shortfall of €41,300 against the branch account.

Under clause 12 of the agreement the subpostmaster is responsible for all losses caused through their own negligence, carelessness or error, and for making good any such loss. I'm not going to pretend this is a small number but the process is the process and I have to record that I've told you.

The system position is the system position. I can't put a figure in front of Dublin that differs from what MERIDIAN says, and neither can you.

Make it good by Friday and we can close it off at branch level. If it goes past Friday it leaves my desk and goes to Security, and neither of us wants that.

Declan Moran
Area Manager, Western Region
s07.mail.gm_002.subject: Re: Branch 4471 Cloghmore — outstanding position
s07.mail.gm_002.body:
Declan,

I have counted the safe every night since the 2nd of March. I have photographed it every night since the 2nd of March. I have the notes and the coin listed separately and I have the times.

Every night my count is right and the terminal is high by between four and six thousand. It goes up on its own overnight. On the 19th I locked the branch at 11:40 with €4,531.40 in the safe and came in at 8:00 to a terminal saying €9,331.40 and nobody in that building but me.

I am not asking you to believe me. I am asking you to send somebody to look at the machine.

Máire
s07.mail.gm_003.subject: Re: Branch 4471 Cloghmore — outstanding position
s07.mail.gm_003.body:
Máire,

I've raised it. The service desk position is that this is an isolated issue at branch level and there is no reported defect matching this behaviour.

I'd gently suggest that going down this road doesn't help you. Branches that dispute the figures don't do better, they just do it slower.

Friday.

Declan

s07.mail.gm_005.subject: Branch audit 4471 — visit report
s07.mail.gm_005.body:
Máire,

As promised, my report went to Dublin on Friday. I've copied you because you asked and because I think you're entitled to it.

Summary: two days on site, full physical count on both days, stock reconciled, remittances checked back six weeks against dockets, safe procedure observed, key control correct.

Finding: no cash, stock or remittance is unaccounted for at this branch. The physical position agrees with the manual records kept by the subpostmaster. It does not agree with the terminal.

I've written the last sentence exactly as I found it and I've been told it is not the sort of finding the report is for. I don't know what happens to it now.

I'm sorry I can't do more than write it down.

Fiona Doyle
Branch Audit
s07.mail.gm_006.subject: MER-2016-0114
s07.mail.gm_006.body:
Mrs Conneely,

You won't get this from the service desk so I'm sending it from my own address and I'd be grateful if you didn't say where it came from.

The behaviour you described to me on the phone on the 24th is a known defect. It has a reference and it has a name. It has been raised eleven times against nine branches since 2014 and I raised four of those myself.

What it does: the overnight reconciliation job re-posts a branch's remittance batch when the job is restarted after a timeout. The branch's balance goes up by the value of the batch. The money does not exist. Nothing is missing from the branch because nothing ever left it.

It is in the Q3 known error log. Your area manager has that log.

I shouldn't be writing this. I've written it anyway.

T. Geraghty
s07.mail.gm_007.subject: Wexford — conviction quashed
s07.mail.gm_007.body:
Máire — I don't know if you remember me, I wrote to you in 2019 and you asked me not to write again, and I've respected that for six years.

I'm writing once more because of what happened in Wexford on Tuesday and then I'll leave you alone.

The Court of Appeal quashed it. The grounds were non-disclosure of material relating to the reliability of the MERIDIAN evidence. That is your case. That is word for word your case.

If you ever want to talk, on or off the record, or not at all, my number hasn't changed.

Eibhlín Ní Chonaill

s07.notes.note_002.title: Procedure
s07.notes.note_002.block_001: Close at 17:30. Cash out of the drawer into the tray.
s07.notes.note_002.block_002: Notes first, in fifties. Coin second, by denomination. Write both figures on the slip.
s07.notes.note_002.block_003: Count it twice. Since March, count it three times.
s07.notes.note_002.block_004: Slip goes in the tray with the notes. Photograph the open safe with the slip visible.
s07.notes.note_002.block_005: Safe photo album passcode is 0203 — the day it started. Do not change it, I will forget it.
s07.notes.note_003.block_001: I am not going to be able to say any of this out loud so I am putting it here.
s07.notes.note_003.block_002: Peadar put in eighteen thousand on Tuesday and would not look at me. He thinks I did it. He paid it anyway. I do not know which of those two things is worse and I have been awake since four working on it.
s07.notes.note_003.block_003: Counsel says the theft count carries prison and the accounting count carries a fine, and that if I plead to the accounting count they will take the theft count. He says a jury will be shown a machine and shown me, and asked which of us they believe.
s07.notes.note_003.block_004: So on Tuesday I am going to stand up in Galway and say a word that is not true, to make a smaller untrue thing happen instead of a bigger one.
s07.notes.note_003.block_005: Twenty-one years I never once took a stamp. Aoife will hear me say it and she will believe it and there is no version of Tuesday where that does not happen.
s07.notes.note_004.title: For after
s07.notes.note_004.block_001: Photographs are in the album called Counts. There are four hundred and sixteen of them.
s07.notes.note_004.block_002: Every one has the slip in it. The slip has the time on it. The safe is open in all of them.
s07.notes.note_004.block_003: The engineer's name is on the email. He was decent and he should not be dragged into it if it can be helped.
s07.notes.note_004.block_004: The audit went to Dublin on the 29th of April and I got a copy because I asked for one at the door.
s07.notes.note_004.block_005: I do not expect anybody to read any of this. I am leaving it tidy because that is what I do.

s07.memos.vm_001.title: 19 March
s07.memos.vm_001.transcript: Right. Saturday the nineteenth of March. Twenty to twelve. Notes, four thousand two hundred and twenty. Coin, three hundred and eleven forty. Total four thousand five hundred and thirty-one forty. And the machine is saying nine thousand three hundred and thirty-one forty. So it wants four thousand eight hundred pounds — euro — four thousand eight hundred euro that is not in this building. There is no four thousand eight hundred in this building. I have counted it three times and I am going to count it once more and then I am going home.
s07.memos.vm_002.title: Service desk
s07.memos.vm_002.transcript: Mrs Conneely, this is the MERIDIAN service desk returning your call of this morning. I have checked with my team leader and I can confirm there are no other branches currently reporting a discrepancy of this type, so this does appear to be an isolated issue at your branch. Unfortunately we are not able to attend site for a variance of this nature. If the shortfall persists you will need to speak to your area manager about making it good. Thanks very much and apologies for any inconvenience.
s07.memos.vm_003.title: 8 May
s07.memos.vm_003.transcript: Tomorrow. I am going to stand up and say it. And the thing I keep coming back to at this hour of the morning is not the money and it is not the nine months. It is that Aoife is going to be sitting there and she is going to hear her mother say it, and after that she will have heard me say it, and I will never be able to unsay it to her. That is the whole of it. That is the whole of what I am buying.

s07.question.q01.title: Twenty to twelve
s07.question.q01.question: For over a year she photographed the same thing every night before she locked up. What is in the photographs?
s07.question.q02.title: Sixty-one calls
s07.question.q02.question: In eleven weeks she rang one number sixty-one times. What is it in her contacts as?
s07.question.q02.opt1: Sort the call log by number
s07.question.q03.title: By Friday
s07.question.q03.question: Her area manager wrote to her three times in a fortnight, and every letter ends with the same instruction. What is she told to do with the shortfall?
s07.question.q03.opt1: Read the thread from Declan Moran
s07.question.q04.title: Follow it
s07.question.q04.question: Forty-one thousand three hundred euro is said to have left that branch. Across every account she has, in the eleven weeks it happened — where did it go?
s07.question.q04.opt1: Open the account summary in Files
s07.question.q05.title: Eleven weeks
s07.question.q05.question: Put the spring of 2016 into the order it happened.
s07.question.q05.ev0: 26–27 April — an auditor spends two days in the branch and counts everything twice
s07.question.q05.ev1: 2 March — the terminal is €4,000 higher than the safe for the first time
s07.question.q05.ev2: 17 May — her brother transfers €18,000 into her account
s07.question.q05.ev3: 20 May — the variance reaches €41,300 and the branch is suspended
s07.question.q05.ev4: 9 March — the first call to the service desk; she is told the issue is isolated
s07.question.q05.ev5: 28 April — an engineer emails her privately with a defect reference
s07.question.q06.title: The word
s07.question.q06.question: She wrote down what the service desk said after every single call, because she was beginning to think she had imagined the last one. They used the same word every time. Which?
s07.question.q07.title: Fourteen miles up the road
s07.question.q07.question: The postmistress in the next village had the same hole in her accounts before Máire ever did. What year?
s07.question.q08.title: Quietly
s07.question.q08.question: Bríd never reported hers. She covered it herself, and it is the reason she could not answer Máire's question. Where did the money come from?
s07.question.q09.title: Four things the company said
s07.question.q09.question: Four statements were put before the court in 2017. Three of them are simply true. Tap the one this phone proves was false when it was made.
s07.question.q09.sn0: The branch terminal recorded a cumulative variance of €41,300 between 2 March and 20 May 2016.
s07.question.q09.sn1: The subpostmaster was the sole keyholder of the branch safe.
s07.question.q09.sn2: No defect was known to the company that could produce a variance of this nature at branch level.
s07.question.q09.sn3: The shortfall was not made good by the subpostmaster within the period allowed under the agreement.
s07.question.q10.title: It has a name
s07.question.q10.question: The fault that did this is listed in a restricted document, with a reference and a name. What is the name?
s07.question.q11.title: Eleven times
s07.question.q11.question: One person raised that fault again and again from inside the company, and then broke the rules to tell her about it. Who?
s07.question.q12.title: Two days on site
s07.question.q12.question: An auditor from head office counted the whole branch twice over two days, and her report never reached the court. What did she find unaccounted for?
s07.question.q13.title: The last photograph
s07.question.q13.question: There are four hundred and sixteen photographs and then there are none. What happened on the day she stopped counting?
s07.question.q13.opt1: Check the date of the last one
s07.question.q14.title: Eighteen thousand
s07.question.q14.question: One person paid a large part of the shortfall out of his own pocket, would not look at her while he did it, and has barely spoken to her since. Who?
s07.question.q15.title: Who had it on his desk
s07.question.q15.question: The restricted log went out to area managers on 8 September 2016. Eight months later somebody who had opened it told her to make the shortfall good by Friday. Name him.

s07.mail.f_gm_121.subject: Wexford — what it means for you
s07.mail.f_gm_121.body: Tuesday's judgment is the first of its kind in this jurisdiction. If you were convicted on evidence from the same system, there is now a route. s07.mail.f_gm_122.subject: Wexford judgment
s07.mail.f_gm_122.body: Dear Mrs Conneely, I acted for you in 2017. I have read Tuesday's judgment and I am writing to you before you read about it anywhere else, because I think you will have questions and I would rather you put them to me than to a newspaper. There is no charge for the conversation and there is no obligation on you at the end of it.

s07.notes.f_note_101.title: Stock
s07.notes.f_note_101.block_001: Order Monday for Thursday. Late order means no stamps by the weekend and the weekend is when they want them.
s07.notes.f_note_101.block_002: Always over-order the N stamps in December and never the W. Learned that the hard way in 1998.
s07.notes.f_note_101.block_003: TV licence forms go faster than anything. Keep a spare bundle under the counter, not in the press.
s07.notes.f_note_101.block_004: Till roll: two boxes, not one. The machine eats it.
s07.notes.f_note_101.block_005: Sign the docket in front of the driver. Never after he has gone.
s07.notes.f_note_102.title: Thursday
s07.notes.f_note_102.block_001: Pension day. Open at half eight, not nine. They are at the door from twenty past.
s07.notes.f_note_102.block_002: Nuala first, always, because of the bus. Then whoever is standing.
s07.notes.f_note_102.block_003: Mind Seán's book. He cannot see the line any more and he will not say it, so turn it round for him and put your thumb where it goes.
s07.notes.f_note_102.block_004: Extra coin on a Thursday. Two hundred in twos, and the same again in fifties.
s07.notes.f_note_111.block_001: Six months. I have not been down the town. Peadar does the shopping in Clifden now and neither of us has said why.
s07.notes.f_note_111.block_002: A woman stopped me at the church and said she was sorry and I could not tell whether she was sorry it happened or sorry I did it, and I did not ask, and I have thought about it every week since.
s07.notes.f_note_111.block_003: That is the thing nobody tells you. It is not the nine months. It is that you never again know what anybody means.
s07.notes.f_note_112.block_001: Three years. I counted the shopping twice today, on the table, in front of Peadar, and I did not know I was doing it until he went out of the room.
s07.notes.f_note_112.block_002: I still wake at ten to four. Twenty-three minutes past eleven and ten to four are the two times of the day that belong to something else now.
s07.notes.f_note_112.block_003: I am not saying any of this to Aoife. She has enough of me as it is.
s07.notes.f_note_113.block_001: The solicitor has written. The girl from the paper has written. There is a crowd with a website who have written twice.
s07.notes.f_note_113.block_002: Nine years I have known exactly what I would say if anybody ever asked me properly, and now three people have asked me properly in one week and I have not opened one of them.
s07.notes.f_note_113.block_003: What frightens me is not being told no again. It is being told yes, and then having to look at Aoife and know what I let her sit through in that room for nothing.
s07.notes.f_note_113.block_004: She is coming Sunday. She has something to ask me. I know what it is.

s07.mail.f2_gm_205.body:
Aoife,

You were twenty when it started and you are thirty-two now and I have never once said thank you for the second row. I have said it about the trains and about the shopping and about the phone calls, but not about the second row, because to say thank you for it I would have to say what you were sitting through.

s07.memos.f2_vm_102.title: After the first day
s07.memos.f2_vm_102.transcript: Well. She was here from nine until twenty past six and she counted every note and every coin in this building with her own two hands, twice, and she did not once look at me the way the rest of them look at me. She is back tomorrow. I have not slept properly since the second of March and I think I might sleep tonight.
s07.memos.f2_vm_103.title: 17 May
s07.memos.f2_vm_103.transcript: He put it in this morning. He did not say anything about it and he did not say anything at the table and he has gone out to the shed. Forty-one years I have known that man and I know the difference between him being quiet and him being quiet at me. I am recording this because I want to be able to prove to myself later that I noticed. That I did not just take it and let him go out to the shed.
s07.memos.f2_vm_104.title: (untitled)
s07.memos.f2_vm_104.transcript: It is ten to three. Right. I am going to say it once, out loud, in my own house, and then I am going to go back to bed. I did not take one penny out of that branch in twenty-one years. Not a stamp. Not a pound. I said a word in a room in Galway that was not true because a man in a wig told me it would cost me less, and it has cost me every single day since, and I would like somebody to have heard me say that. There. That is it. Back to bed.

Nine years I have had the answer ready. Nine years. And now that somebody is at the door with the question I am sitting in the dark at quarter past four in the morning talking into a telephone. What I am afraid of is not that they say no. I have had no. What I am afraid of is that they say yes and then I have to look at Aoife and tell her what that room was for.

s07.notes.f2_note_211.block_002: It is not that they think I did it. Half of them do not. It is that I said I did, so nobody can defend me without calling me a liar, and nobody will do that to my face. So they say nothing kind and they say nothing cruel and they cross the road.
s07.notes.f2_note_211.block_003: I built that trap and I stood in it. Nobody put me there.
s07.notes.f2_note_212.block_001: Aoife had the radio on about the English ones. I turned it off and I said nothing to her about why.
s07.notes.f2_note_212.block_002: The reason is not what she thinks. It is not that I cannot bear to hear it.
s07.notes.f2_note_212.block_003: It is that every one of those people said they were innocent, and kept saying it, for years, to anybody who would listen, and that is why there is a programme about them.
